title: B2 · L10 — Inversion in conditionals
description: Inversión formal en condicionales: 'Had I known...', 'Were I to accept...', 'Should you need...'. Registro literario y profesional.

questions.prompt: Reescribes una frase para un email formal de disculpa.
questions.question: Rewrite: 'If I had known, I would have called.'
options: Would I have known, I would have called.
Had I known, I would have called.
If had I known, I would have called.
Known I had, I would have called.
questions.explanation: En tercer condicional formal, se OMITE 'if' y se invierte 'had + sujeto'. La opción C es un error clásico: si eliminas 'if', no lo vuelvas a meter delante de la inversión. Es un recurso elegante y compacto — nativos lo usan en emails cuidados, discursos y escritura formal.
examples: Had she asked me directly, I would've helped without hesitation. → email profesional
Had we left the airport earlier, we wouldn't have missed the connection.

questions.prompt: Redactas un consejo formal en una carta al director.
questions.question: Rewrite: 'If I were you, I would apologise.'
options: Was I you, I would apologise.
Were I you, I would apologise.
If were I you, I would apologise.
Would I you, I apologise.
questions.explanation: El segundo condicional con 'were' invierte a 'Were I + complemento'. La inversión SOLO funciona con 'were' (nunca con 'was', ni con otros verbos como 'had' en segundo condicional). Error típico: usar 'was' invertido — es agramatical incluso si en inglés casual 'if I was' se acepta.
examples: Were I in your position, I would resign immediately. → consejo firme y formal
Were she to accept the offer, the whole team dynamic would change.

questions.statement: 'Should you need help, please call me' es una forma formal de decir 'If you need help'.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Should' invertido sustituye a 'if' en el primer condicional formal, añadiendo un matiz de eventualidad remota o cortesía extra. Es fórmula omnipresente en cartas de negocios, emails corporativos, contratos y anuncios oficiales. En hablado casual sonaría rígido.
examples: Should you have any questions, feel free to contact us at any time. → cierre de email formal
Should the item arrive damaged, please return it within 14 days for a full refund.

questions.text: Should you require further assistance, do not hesitate to contact our customer service team.
questions.explanation: Frase estándar de correspondencia comercial y firma de email. Prosodia neutra y profesional. Connected speech: 'should you' se enlaza 'ʃʊd-ju', y 'do not' en registro formal se pronuncia completo (no 'don't') para mantener el tono. 'Hesitate to contact' se fusiona con la /t/ suave.
examples: Should you wish to cancel your subscription, please provide 24 hours' notice.
Should any issues arise during the setup, contact our technical support team.

questions.prompt: Redactas un párrafo condicional en una propuesta de negocio.
questions.question: Which is correct inversion in a second conditional?
options: Were he to arrive early, he could join us.
Was he to arrive early, he could join us.
If were he to arrive, he could join us.
Would he arrive early, he could join us.
questions.explanation: 'Were + sujeto + to + infinitivo' es una fórmula formal para condicionales hipotéticos poco probables. Sustituye a 'If he were to arrive'. Aporta un matiz aún más formal que 'Were I you', y es típica en contratos, propuestas y análisis de riesgo. NUNCA se usa 'was' en esta estructura invertida.
examples: Were they to accept our proposal, we would proceed with implementation next quarter.
Were she to leave the company, the entire product roadmap would need rethinking.

questions.statement: La inversión en condicionales solo funciona con cláusulas 'if' en pasado.
questions.explanation: FALSO. La inversión funciona con tres tipos de condicionales: (1) tercer condicional ('Had I known'), (2) segundo condicional con 'were' ('Were I' / 'Were he to'), y (3) primer condicional con 'should' ('Should you need'). No funciona con condicional cero (verdades generales) ni con segundo condicional con otros verbos.
examples: Present/future: Should you have any questions, let me know.
Past hypothetical: Had I realised the mistake sooner, I could've fixed it.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada inversión condicional con su cláusula lógica:

pairs.left: Were I to accept the offer,
Were it not for your help,

questions.explanation: Cada inversión pertenece a un tipo distinto: 'Had...' (tercer condicional), 'Were... to' (segundo condicional formal), 'Should you...' (primer condicional formal), 'Had ... not' (tercer condicional negativo), 'Were it not for' (fórmula fija para expresar gratitud/dependencia). Memoriza cada patrón como bloque completo.
examples: Had I not seen it with my own eyes, I wouldn't have believed a word of it.
Were it not for sheer luck, we wouldn't have made the deadline.

questions.prompt: Expresas gratitud formal por el consejo de una mentora.
questions.question: Complete: '___ it not been for her advice, I would have made a huge mistake.'
options: If
Should
Had
Were
questions.explanation: 'Had it not been for' = 'If it hadn't been for'. Es la fórmula elegante para expresar gratitud o dependencia respecto a circunstancias pasadas que evitaron algo malo. Muy usada en agradecimientos formales, discursos, memorias. La versión presente/hipotética sería 'Were it not for'.
examples: Had it not been for the paramedics' quick response, he wouldn't have survived. → nota de agradecimiento
Had it not been for the pandemic, we would've launched the product two years ago.

questions.target: Should you decide to accept our offer, we would be delighted to have you join the team.
questions.explanation: Frase estándar de carta de oferta laboral. Registro cortés y profesional. Prosodia: ritmo pausado, sin contracciones ('would' no 'we'd'). 'We would be delighted' es una colocación formal fija más elegante que 'we'd be happy'. Nativos añaden 'sincerely' o 'genuinely' antes de 'delighted' para intensificar sin sonar impostado.
examples: Should you wish to proceed with the agreement, kindly sign and return the enclosed documents.
Should you require any clarification regarding the terms, please contact us directly.

questions.prompt: Un abogado da un consejo formal a un cliente.
questions.question: Which structure is used for polite formal advice?
options: Had I been you...
Were I you...
Would I be you...
Should I be you...
questions.explanation: 'Were I you' es la versión invertida y formal de 'If I were you'. Aporta un matiz elevado, casi literario. Común en textos de asesoramiento formal, cartas de opinión y consejos elegantes. En conversación casual siempre 'If I were you' o 'If I were in your shoes'.
examples: Were I you, I would reconsider that decision very carefully before signing.
Were I in your shoes, I would seek independent legal advice first.

questions.statement: 'Had he been more careful, this accident wouldn't have happened' usa la inversión correctamente.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Es un tercer condicional invertido perfecto: 'Had he been' = 'If he had been'. El uso del pasivo ('been more careful') añade formalidad. Esta construcción enfatiza la reflexión sobre las consecuencias evitables — muy común en informes de accidente, análisis post-mortem y crónicas periodísticas.
examples: Had she been more prepared for the interview, she would have got the offer.
Had they invested wisely in their 20s, they would be financially free by now.

questions.text: Were it not for the quick response of the paramedics, he might not have survived.
questions.explanation: 'Were it not for' + 'might not have + PP' — combinación elegante para hablar de tragedias evitadas. Prosodia solemne, típica de crónica periodística seria. Connected speech: 'were it' se enlaza 'wɜːr-ɪt', y 'not have' se pronuncia con 'not' débil, casi glotalizada.
examples: Were it not for sheer luck, we would've been stranded on that mountain overnight.
Were it not for her patience with me, I would've quit that job months ago.

questions.prompt: Reescribes una frase para el pie de un contrato.
questions.question: Which is the formal equivalent of 'If you should have any concerns'?
options: Have you any concerns
Should you have any concerns
Had you any concerns
Were you any concerns
questions.explanation: Se omite 'if' y se invierte 'should + sujeto': 'Should you have any concerns'. Es fórmula omnipresente en comunicación empresarial, condiciones de servicio, notificaciones bancarias. Aporta un matiz de cortesía extra que reconoce la posibilidad remota pero real de que surja algo.
examples: Should you have any doubts about the procedure, please raise them before signing.
Should the flight be delayed by more than two hours, you'll be notified by SMS.

questions.target: Had I been given the opportunity earlier in my career, I might have pursued a different path entirely.
questions.explanation: Reflexión formal sobre el pasado, típica de entrevistas biográficas, memorias o charlas TED. Combina inversión ('Had I been given') con pasiva y modal condicional ('might have pursued') — registro reflexivo y ligeramente literario. Prosodia: pausas contemplativas, énfasis en 'entirely'. Nativos añaden hedging: 'you know', 'I sometimes wonder'.
examples: Had I studied medicine as my parents wanted, my life would look completely different today.
Had I accepted that international transfer back then, I'd probably be based in Singapore now.

questions.prompt: Identifica qué frase no admite inversión.
questions.question: Which sentence CANNOT be inverted?
options: If I had known, I would have called.
If I were rich, I would travel.
If you should need help, call me.
If I like coffee, I drink it.
questions.explanation: El condicional CERO ('If + presente + presente' para verdades generales o hábitos) NO admite inversión. La inversión sólo funciona con condicionales hipotéticos (2 y 3) o con 'should' en primer condicional formal. Regla clave: si la oración expresa causa-efecto real y siempre cierta, olvídate de invertir.
examples: Cannot invert: If water reaches 100°C, it boils. → verdad universal
Can invert: Had I known about the leak, I would have acted immediately.
